title: Chatway MCP: Tools, Pricing and Setup (2026 Guide)
summary: Chatway MCP is now available for AI automation workflows. You can determine which existing integrations are supported and what updates your system…
body_markdown:
## Connecting Chatway MCP in a workflow today


As of 2026-10-15, the builder has no native Chatway MCP integration. You reach it through three generic building blocks. Given the small trial allowance, the cheapest one to test should go first.


The table compares them. Take from it that the effort rises with each route, and so does what you must confirm in Chatway's docs.


Route Setup effort Needs from Chatway docs When it fits Not run by us


HTTP request step Low Endpoint URL, auth header, request body shape One fixed call Yes


AI step, custom provider Medium Whether Chatway exposes a compatible model endpoint Only if the docs describe one Yes


MCP server connection Medium to high Server URL, transport type, auth method An agent choosing among Chatway tools Yes


We haven't run any of these against Chatway. Each row is a plan drawn from the maker's pages, not a result.


Call one documented endpoint with a fixed payload. You need the exact URL and header format from Chatway, and nothing else. Use it when the job is a single predictable action.


Only if Chatway publishes an endpoint speaking an OpenAI-compatible format does route 2, an AI step with a custom provider, work. If the docs describe an MCP server and nothing more, this route has nothing to connect to.


A transport is simply how an MCP client and server talk to each other: either as a local process on your machine (stdio) or over a remote HTTP-based connection (streamable HTTP, or the older SSE).


The three columns in the matrix below run in that order: stdio, streamable HTTP, SSE.


To find which one Chatway documents, look in its tool reference and setup pages for how the server is reached, since a command to launch points to stdio and a server URL points to a remote HTTP transport.


That matters for a client like ChatGPT, which lacks stdio, so a Chatway server offered only as a local process would not connect there.


With route 3, an MCP server connection, the question is transport. ConnectorZone's[client matrix](https://connector.zone/tools/client-matrix/) scores each client on three transports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code score 1, 1, 1.


ChatGPT scores 0, 1, 1. So ChatGPT lacks the first transport, and a server offering only that one won't connect there. Check which transport Chatway documents before choosing a client.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) exposes each project as its own MCP server, so Claude, Cursor or Windsurf can create the HTTP request flow, change it and explain it back to you with no builder UI open.


That is real create-and-edit control over an open protocol, not a chat box describing a screen it can't touch, and the tool calls and resulting changes land in the run trace for you to read after asking for a Chatway call.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces, and its core is MIT-licensed.
